europe_cited.title: A review of IRS-assisted communication for medical robotics: enabling intelligent wireless control in 6G healthcare systems
europe_cited.authors: Zhang, Siwen, Saleem, Asad, Zhou, Liang, Meiling, Sun, Komolafe, Temitope E., Xu, Yan
europe_cited.abstract: Advances in wireless communication are reshaping medical robotics by enabling more responsive and connected healthcare systems. This review article examines how millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), and massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) can support the closed-loop, latency-sensitive, and reliability-critical requirements of medical robotic systems. Rather than treating these technologies as separate wireless trends, the paper analyzes their complementary roles in robotic sensing, control feedback, mobility support, and resilient connectivity across applications such as telesurgery, patient monitoring, rehabilitation, and smart hospital robotics. Particular emphasis is placed on sixth-generation (6G) capabilities, AI-driven wireless adaptation, and communication-robotics co-design under constraints including blockage, interference, device miniaturization, power limits, and cybersecurity. Key implementation barriers, open challenges, and future research directions are also summarized.

europe_cited.abstract: With the development of 6G networks, drones have been widely used in the field of wireless communication due to their high mobility and flexible deployment. europe_cited.abstract: This paper analyzes the physical layer security of Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) networks with Full Duplex Energy Harvesting (FD EH) and Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) with the aim of enhancing spectrum efficiency and reliability. europe_cited.title: The Road Towards RIS Standardization
europe_cited.authors: Liu, Ruiqi, Shojaeifard, Arman, Wu, Qingqing, Liu, Yuanwei, Di Renzo, Marco, Alexandropoulos, George C.
europe_cited.journal: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Wireless Communications
europe_cited.abstract: As a vital component of smart and sustainable radio environment, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) plays a critical role in future wireless communications systems. The abilities of RIS to alter wireless propagation conditions with lower cost of deployment and lower energy consumption make it a strong candidate technology for the next generation networks. Given these merits studied by the academia, the industrial community has taken steps to standardize RIS in order to harmonize it with the current system design. The ETSI ISG RIS is one of the earliest standardization group to study RIS and their activities are provided in details. Particularly, a variety of use cases and deployment scenarios are identified, modelling of RIS-assisted communication channels is studied, and reference archetectures and future standardization impact are also analyzed. The future of RIS standardization lies in the industrial consensus to mature this technology further and address its engineering challenges.

europe_cited.title: UAV-Assisted Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Channel State Information Prediction in Beyond 5G Communication Systems: A Machine Learning Perspective
europe_cited.authors: Djakwah, Peter, Ahado, William Mawuli, Annor, Andrew Essah Owiredu, Amadu, Aminatu, Achiaa, Akua, Mensah, Clerance Abraham, Agyemang, Justice Owusu, Gadze, James Dzisi
europe_cited.journal: Pan-African Artificial Intelligence and Smart Systems
europe_cited.abstract: This research presents a novel deep learning framework for channel state information (CSI) prediction in UAV-assisted Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) enabled Beyond 5G (B5G) communication systems. The proposed approach leverages a hybrid 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture to capture both spatial and temporal dependencies inherent in dynamic wireless environments. Simulated in MATLAB, the model utilizes Rician fading channels, user and UAV mobility patterns, and real-time environmental parameters to generate CSI datasets. This dataset is fed into the 3D-CNN + LSTM model to predict CSI. The results demonstrate rapid convergence, low RMSE (0.12–0.18), and high prediction accuracy (up to 88%). The predicted sum-rate closely aligns with ground truth across varying SNR levels, validating the model’s capacity to preserve spectral efficiency under dynamic conditions. Future work will look into optimizing the performance of the model and benchmarking it against other CSI prediction methods .
